comparison: Perfect agreement on C. elegans connectome data (C2, C11, C12, C60, C61, C62). Both evaluations accept the data source as valid and well-documented, though peer reviewers question the choice to use C. elegans rather than directly studying the inferior olive system.

Perfect agreement on theoretical foundation (C16, C17, C18). Both evaluations accept the underlying physics concepts of wave properties and Anderson localization as well-established, though peer reviewers question their application to the biological system.
Agreement on background claims about inferior olive (C1, C8, C9, C10). Both evaluations accept these as established prior work with appropriate citations, providing valid context for the study.

Agreement on the absence of confirmed subthreshold oscillations in C. elegans (C15, C57 overlap). Both evaluations acknowledge this as an established fact, though they differ on implications - OpenEval sees it as important context while peer reviewers see it as a fundamental limitation.

Strong disagreement on circuit model construction methodology (C64, C65, C66, C67, C68). OpenEval finds the virtual node insertion clearly justified and mathematically coherent, while peer reviewers challenge this choice as altering the network structure without clear justification.

Disagreement on tight-binding approximation (C72, C73, C74, C75). OpenEval finds the theoretical framework well-established and properly adapted, while peer reviewers express significant doubt about whether this approximation is justified and question if findings may be artifacts of the modeling approach.

Disagreement on parameter choice (C78, C79). OpenEval finds the γ=5 parameter justified through preliminary analysis, while peer reviewers criticize this as part of broader concerns about arbitrary parameter selections lacking motivation.

Partial disagreement on threshold behavior and mobility edge (C3, C25, C26, C29). OpenEval finds the signal mobility edge definition reasonable and supported by data, while peer reviewers question whether the mobility edges are artifacts of the tight-binding approximation rather than meaningful biological results.

Both address transmission patterns at mobility edge (C29 overlap). OpenEval finds the observations directly supported by heatmap data, while peer reviewers question the validity due to concerns about the underlying approximation.

Disagreement on wavenumber-dependent transmission maps (C30, C32, C33, C34). OpenEval finds the selection criteria justified and patterns supported by data, while peer reviewers question whether findings depend strongly on virtual node additions and may not be valid.

Disagreement on regular transmission patterns (C4, C35, C36). OpenEval finds patterns consistent with linear strand structure and wave interference principles, while peer reviewers question validity due to methodological concerns about virtual nodes.

Disagreement on major hub identification (C5, C45, C46, C48, C50, C51). OpenEval finds the threshold definition reasonable and mechanistic explanation physically sound, while peer reviewers question the biological significance given inadequate evidence for interference effects being a major component.

Disagreement on interference vs. non-interference model contrast (C55, C56 overlap, plus C47). OpenEval finds the evidence clear and physically consistent, while peer reviewers state the strength of evidence for interference effects is inadequate and conclusions lack empirical grounding.

Agreement that extrapolation to inferior olive is problematic (C58, C59). OpenEval marks as uncertain noting speculation remains untested, while peer reviewers more strongly reject the claim, stating authors should provide more evidence or refrain from making this conclusion.

OpenEval finds computational analysis scope and parameters (C19, C20, C21, C22) comprehensive and clearly specified. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological claims about calculation scope.

OpenEval finds transparent reporting of computational errors (C80, C81, C82) strengthens the work with minimal error rate and reasonable corrections. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific error reporting claims.

OpenEval finds the role of hmc and distance characteristics (C37-C44) well-documented with specific neuron examples. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these bridging function claims, though related hub findings are questioned in R9.
